title: An Apple silicon host runs the published sandbox image under emulation, because only amd64 is published and nothing checks
foundBy: session agent, answering the maintainer's question "in codesweep-ai are we able to publish arm64 images?", 2026-09-14

evidence.verified:
`go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/ ./internal/doctor/ ./internal/engine/` passes, and all nine new tests pass with it. With the call sites in create.go, misc_commands.go and doctor.go reverted, four of them fail: TestBuildBuildsWhenThePullBroughtAnotherPlatform, TestEnsureImageRefusesAPullForAnotherPlatform, TestEnsureImageSaysAnUnfetchableImageIsTheWrongPlatform and TestDiagnoseImageForAnotherPlatform.

End to end on an x86_64 host with podman 5.8.2, CS_SANDBOX_IMAGE named `docker.io/arm64v8/busybox:1.28`, stored as linux/arm64 on a linux/amd64 engine. `doctor` reported that pair and named `cs-sandbox build`. `create` exited 1 saying `the registry has no linux/amd64 image of it`, and made no sandbox. The same image tagged under localhost/ was reported present. `make check` exited 0 on the change.

resolution: `build`, `create` and `doctor` now compare the platform of the image in the local store with the platform podman's server runs, which on macOS is the podman machine. `build` builds a pulled image for another platform again, natively from the tiers. `create` fetches it again, and fails naming `build` when the registry has no image for this platform. An image under localhost/ is exempt. SPEC R165 holds the rule.
details:
The images a sandbox runs are published for linux/amd64 alone. `skopeo inspect --raw` on `ghcr.io/codesweep-ai/sandbox:v0.0.0-20260911220608-fe9796dafc77` and on its `sandbox-slim` twin returns a single OCI manifest whose config says linux/amd64. The tiers under them are lists of amd64 and arm64. The `publish-images` job in ci.yml builds on ubuntu-26.04 only.

Podman does not refuse such an image on another architecture. On podman 5.8.2, `podman pull --arch arm64 docker.io/amd64/busybox:1.28` prints `WARNING: image platform (linux/amd64) does not match the expected platform (linux/arm64)`, exits 0, and stores linux/amd64. That was measured on an x86_64 host asking for arm64, not on a Mac.

cs-sandbox never asks. `build` reads a successful pull as the image, and `create` reads `podman image exists` the same way. So on Apple silicon both settle for the amd64 image rather than building a native one from the arm64 tiers. The base-images workflow records what that costs. Under emulation, all four claude replay members timed out at 10.5s against 5.5s native.

notes.text: Commit 37a4b02 publishes linux/arm64 beside linux/amd64 under each version tag, so an arm64 host will pull its own image rather than build it. That half has not run in CI yet. Versions published before it stay amd64 only.
